extracted.intended_audience: Department of Defense contracting officers, installation commanders, and researchers/practitioners working on A-76 competitive sourcing studies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for conducting DoD competitive sourcing (OMB A-76) studies, preparing solicitation documents (PWS/QASP), developing the Most Efficient Organization (MEO)/Management Plan, performing cost comparisons, and addressing institutional/legal risks. Focus is on execution and assessment of A-76 competitions at installations/commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Work Statement (PWS) definition and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: A Performance Work Statement is a statement of the technical, functional and performance characteristics of the work to be performed; identifies essential functions to be performed; determines performance factors, including the location of the work, the units of work, the quantity of work units, and the quality and timeliness of the work units. It serves as the scope of the work and the basis for all costs. [Ref. 10]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PWS must accurately reflect all activities involved in the operation because it is the basis for proposal evaluation, the in-house estimate and the MEO. It must be developed so it does not limit service operations, arbitrarily increase risk, reduce competition, violate industry/service norms, or omit statutory/regulatory requirements. A PWS should be performance-oriented (state outputs/measures and limiting directions) and should not indicate how a supplier must accomplish the service. Poorly trained teams produce poor PWS language, leading to weak evaluation criteria, legal vulnerability, poor performance and cost increases. Contracting Officer oversight during acquisition strategy development is a control point to catch discrepancies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP) content and relationship to PWS
rubrics_metrics.description: The QASP describes the methods of inspections to be used, the reports required and the resources to be expended; it is designed to complement the PWS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: QASP need not be published in the solicitation nor provided to Government employees developing the management study; competing sources (including the management plan) are expected to develop a QASP based solely on the requirements outlined in the PWS. QASP should align to PWS performance standards and measures and specify inspection/reporting methods and resource allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management Plan / Most Efficient Organization (MEO) completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: The Management Plan detailing the Government's Most Efficient Organization is the basis for the Government's in-house cost estimate; it should reflect the scope of the PWS and identify the organizational structure needed to meet the outlined requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Management Plan must document best structure, staffing, operating procedures, equipment, and inspection plans to ensure in-house activity is performed effectively and cost-efficiently. It must also document assumptions used in developing the MEO and the in-house cost estimate, including organizational assets, QASP, Transition Plan and the in-house cost estimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation compliance and handling (IFB/RFP and security)
rubrics_metrics.description: The solicitation must be issued through appropriate channels in accordance with the FAR, Service regulations and any other applicable statutory requirements; depending on the nature of services, either an Invitation For Bid (IFB) or a Request For Proposal (RFP) can be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals received should be treated the same as other competitions with regard to the security of each offer submitted. Ensure solicitation follows applicable procurement rules and preserves fairness and confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost comparison procedure and evaluation (sealed bids and negotiated procurements)
rubrics_metrics.description: In sealed bids the Contracting Officer opens all bids (including the in-house estimate) and records prices on the Cost Comparison Form; tentative decision is announced based on these data subject to evaluation for responsiveness and responsibility. In negotiated or best-value procurements, the most advantageous private sector or ISSA proposal is compared against the in-house estimate on the Cost Comparison Form and award is made as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comparisons must consider responsiveness/responsibility. For best value procurements, trade-offs between contractor proposals and Government MEO should be evaluated and MEO may modify operations/bid to meet best value criteria before re-comparing costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Savings threshold for awarding commercial activities to contractors
rubrics_metrics.description: For a commercial activity to be awarded to a contractor, the contractor's bid must meet a savings threshold of 10 percent of personnel costs or $10 million over the performance period. If the threshold is not met, the activity remains in-house. [Ref. 13:p. 24]
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the threshold strictly when determining whether outsourcing is economically justified. In best-value scenarios, other non-cost trade-offs may alter outcome but threshold is a baseline economic criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardization and method for capturing Government operating costs
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no standard currently used to measure Government operating costs across DoD; the supplement to OMB A-76 provides guidance but is often silent on calculating some costs. DoD has looked to implement Activity Based Costing (ABC) for capturing costs of performing commercial activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose and document a consistent costing methodology (ABC recommended) that truly captures total costs of providing a particular service. Incomplete/casual cost capture leads to hidden costs and post-award price adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness and quality of cost-capturing in the PWS
rubrics_metrics.description: The ability to accurately capture costs is tied to the development of the PWS, as it defines what costs must be captured and included in the competitive proposal submitted by the MEO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the PWS captures all expected work. Hidden costs often arise from a poorly constructed PWS, increasing contract total cost after award. Reviews of contracted services show mixed ability of Government to capture costs through PWS; completeness is a critical success factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and identification of commercial activities vs inherently Governmental functions
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB A-76 lists numerous functions that qualify as commercial services but there is no consensus among Services/commanders on what constitutes a commercial activity or an inherently Governmental function; comprehensive list of eligible commercial activities provided in Appendix B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commands should develop clear, consistent definitions and consolidated lists (e.g., across major commands) per FAIR Act requirements; lack of clarity impedes selection of functions for study and consistent application of A-76.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study timeframes and schedule adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Current A-76 timeframes: single activity studies must be completed within 18 months, multi-service studies within 36 months, although past averages were much longer (approx. 4 years, 3 months for FY87–90).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize these timeframes are ambitious; plans should account for realistic staffing and scheduling. Shortening timeframes could affect study quality; monitor start/completion delays and plan resources accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and qualification of personnel to conduct studies
rubrics_metrics.description: The greatest concern in completing studies on time is availability of personnel familiar with A-76; downsizing has reduced experienced uniform and civilian staff able to conduct studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider outsourcing parts of the A-76 study while retaining in-house cost estimate and inherently Governmental functions. Ensure retained staff have requisite experience; provide training to PWS teams and assign experienced personnel to key roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee participation incentives and conflict-of-interest constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: There is difficulty in getting experienced civil service employees to participate in PWS development due to concerns about job loss and legal restrictions preventing displaced employees from working for the contractor who wins the contract for two years if they participated in the study as a 'procurement official.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate low volunteer rates; design participation rules to respect legal restrictions and mitigate perverse incentives. Use non-attribution surveys or other methods to gather input; ensure transparency and fairness to minimize sabotage risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional commitment and leadership continuity
rubrics_metrics.description: Short tours of duty for base commanders limit institutional knowledge and often result in focus on short-term projects rather than major long-term base operation changes; commanders may fear loss of control over services and be reluctant to negotiate with contractors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build institutional commitment at multiple levels, document institutional knowledge, and engage leaders to accept changes. Address commander concerns about control and family welfare when considering outsourcing of base services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safeguards against misrepresentation and oversight responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: There is potential (though unlikely) for A-76 team members to misrepresent information to protect jobs; oversight by the Contracting Officer during acquisition strategy development is the primary control to catch discrepancies in the PWS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement oversight checkpoints, audits and independent reviews of PWS and MEO assumptions. Document assumptions and require justification; include checks to detect intentional or inadvertent misrepresentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal and statutory restrictions on outsourcing specific activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific legal restrictions prohibit outsourcing certain services (e.g., firefighting and policing aboard installations) and congressional mandates may require a percentage of depot maintenance be performed by Government employees. Past Defense Authorization Acts contained language restricting contracting based on cost-comparison results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before initiating studies or solicitations, review current authorization/appropriation law and statutes to identify prohibitions or set-asides. Ensure compliance with public laws and OMB A-76 constraints; account for legislative changes that may affect eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and evaluation metrics to collect from commands (survey-style metrics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey questions used in the study indicate useful monitoring metrics: number of competitive sourcing studies undertaken; number resulting in MEO vs contractor/ISSA competition or direct conversion; which group determined eligible commercial activities; existence of lists excluding activities from competition; general and specific nature of services studied; whether cost comparisons were performed and reasons if not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commands should track and report these metrics to evaluate A-76 implementation effectiveness and lessons learned. Use consistent definitions when collecting data (e.g., what counts as a study, what constitutes direct conversion).
